verifiable-quality-gates.why: the fix is a merge-config change whose effect must be proven, not asserted; the test must fail if the attribute is dropped.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added test/union-merge.test.mjs - union resolves two appends (both lines, no markers), the same merge conflicts WITHOUT the attribute (control), and git check-attr confirms all three real paths resolve to merge=union.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

architectural-decision-records.why: a deliberate change to the repo's merge strategy with a non-obvious scope rule (never code) and honest limits.
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0087 (extend union to CHANGELOG.md, the one shared file not already covered; scope union to accumulating text only).
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the risk is git's merge behavior, so the test exercises a real two-branch merge at the level that owns it.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: an integration test that builds a throwaway git repo, creates a conflicting two-append merge, and asserts union auto-resolves it (plus the no-union control and the check-attr resolution).
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug, and match the test type to the risk.

skeptical-audit.why: the ADR claims the conflicts are 'gone' and names what union does not cover; those claims need an evidence state and a named limitation.
skeptical-audit.what: stated the honest limits in ADR-0087 (byte-identical duplicate lines, unguaranteed hunk order, union scoped to the listed files only, never source code) and proved the mechanism rather than asserting it.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: a change to the repo's merge configuration (which could silently clobber the existing .gitattributes or mis-scope union to code) must pass the four-questions review before done.
judge-arch.what: ran a fresh-context subagent review of the staged diff, specifically that .gitattributes is purely additive and union is not applied to any code pattern; recorded in docs/arch-reviews/log.jsonl.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the change is a .mjs test that enumerates the merge-driver behavior by case (the coupling rule treats a changed .mjs as a behavior surface); the happy, adverse, and boundary cases are all covered.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: node:test cases: union auto-resolves two appends (happy), the same merge conflicts WITHOUT the attribute (adverse control), and git check-attr confirms all three real paths resolve to merge=union (boundary).
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: no input, auth, secret, or file-handling control; a merge-driver config change.

pattern-selector.why: no design pattern; a one-line .gitattributes rule.

arch-encode.why: no new recurring rule file; the behavior is pinned by its own discrimination test.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, storage, migration, retention, or backup is touched.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no system/data architecture or service-boundary change; repo merge config.

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy mechanics, migration, flag, or rollback change.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, SLO, alert, or golden signal.
